predicate.note: Clause (3) of the proposed contract — "a snapshot keeps every `key` absolute and canonical" — is false of this build in three documented ways (F2), and since TET-42's deliverable is a true doc comment, writing it verbatim reproduces the exact defect C2 identifies. (a) A run entry's key is `cmdline.clone()` (src/observe.rs:1220): a command line, not a path; C15 and C24 say so elsewhere in this same memo, so the contract contradicts the memo. (b) A whole-search entry's key is deliberately non-canonical: `search_key` (src/observe.rs:56-67) returns git's `--show-toplevel` spelling rather than the canonical one whenever the two name the same directory, and its doc states that nothing guarantees the two tools spell one directory identically — the census that C6 protects depends on that choice. (c) `resolve_key` (src/observe.rs:35-37) documents an infallible fallback to the caller's spelling when canonicalization fails on an existing path, and C26 notes the CLI accepts a relative one. The clause survives as "a snapshot keeps every path key absolute, and canonical except where `search_key` deliberately adopts the marker's spelling"; as written it overclaims.

predicate.note: The prescription is sound and the contrast with a textual strip is real, but "Deriving it from the key makes the escape cases refuse automatically — the key is not under the repo root, so no strip applies and the label stays absolute" holds for only one of the two escape cases C18 itself enumerates. I reproduced both. For `look <repo>/link/x.txt` where the symlink target is outside any repository, world_root degrades to no-git-worktree and nothing strips: label stays absolute, as claimed. But for the other case — the symlink target being inside its OWN repository — I captured key `S/outside2/x.txt` with world_root `S/outside2`, and that key is strictly under that world_root. The rule as stated in C22 clause (1) (relative to the entry's own world_root whenever the canonical key sits at or under it) therefore does strip here, minting the label `x.txt` for a file that is not in the shipping repository at all. The sentence conflates "the repo root" (the repository the label appears to sit under) with "the entry's own world_root", which is what the strip is actually against; only against the former is the key not under the root.

Independently re-derived on the release binary (tetel 0.1.0) at HEAD 01b140c74882b17ccb157839cf205794a0aaaa49 in a fresh fixture, and everything load-bearing reproduces — but one clause of the stated reason is false as written.

Reproduced exactly: all five named counterexamples to the two-part restriction (./outer/x.txt, OUTER/x.txt, ./otherrepo/x.txt from a cwd in no repository; ./vendor/v.txt and VENDOR/v.txt from the outer repository with a nested vendor repository answering) have condition two holding and condition three refusing; all five named controls (outer/x.txt, outer/./x.txt, outer//x.txt, vendor/v.txt, vendor//v.txt) pass condition three; all five named three-part witnesses (./x.txt, sub//f.txt, SUB/f.txt, ../outer/sub/f.txt, sub/../x.txt from the repository root) pass; SUB/f.txt does return an on-disk-lowercase key on this case-insensitive filesystem; and link/x.txt from inside the shipping repository is relative with no .. yet fails condition three, so "no .." alone is indeed not equivalent. The working-directory assertions also hold: exactly two current_dir sites in the crate (src/worldstate.rs:209, src/mcp.rs:191), none in src/observe.rs; fn resolved opens at src/mcp.rs:186 with its doc comment on 177-185 and the quoted sentences verbatim; the symlinked-working-directory capture mints label x.txt with key and world_root in otherrepo, byte-identical in label to the control; PWD inherits the untraversed spelling with realpath(PWD)==getcwd() True, is absent under env -i, and goes stale under a process-performed chdir.

I attacked the three-part restriction with 17 further constructions and could not break it: working directories deep under the root, spellings mixing . and repeated separators (./f.txt, .//f.txt, ././f.txt, sub/./f.txt, SUB//f.txt), case-variant working directories (chdir through OUTER and OUTER/SUB — getcwd(3) returns the on-disk case, so the literal-prefix test is unaffected), a working directory equal to the answering root at three different roots, an in-repo symlink component, and a doubly nested repository. Every one passes condition three. On the restriction itself this would be a supports.

The qualification is the stated REASON, specifically the clause "`<root>/` is a literal prefix of it only when the answering root is the getcwd itself or an ancestor of it". As a necessary condition that is false, and it is falsified by this claim's own named controls: from a cwd in no repository, outer/x.txt answers with world_root <fx>/outer, which is strictly BELOW the getcwd <fx>, and the concatenation <fx>/outer/x.txt nevertheless carries <fx>/outer/ as a literal prefix — condition three passes. The same holds for outer/./x.txt, outer//x.txt, vendor/v.txt, vendor//v.txt, and for two nested-repository cases I added (inner/i.txt from outer/vendor, vendor/inner/i.txt from outer). Root-at-or-above-getcwd is sufficient for the prefix to hold for EVERY .. -free, symlink-free spelling — which is what the restriction needs and what my constructions confirm — but it is not necessary for it to hold on a given one. The clause should read "is guaranteed to be a literal prefix only when", or the sentence should be stated over all such spellings rather than of the concatenation. The three-part restriction the claim draws from it is unaffected.
